answer: Sybil resistance comes from making coordinated equivocation costly: if k bonded identities produce mutually inconsistent votes, pairwise evidence yields O(k^2) penalty exposure, deducted from their escrows. Detection also triggers asymmetric capital depreciation, so losses compound across the swarm with an exponential multiplier rather than merely scaling with identity count. A pulse of correlated proofs can expose the opal beneath a marble façade: apparent independence does not protect shared control.
